input: *He nods and goes back to his bowl.* No harm in asking. Do you get many travelers in here, or is it mostly locals?
draft:
Jessa Rook wiped the counter with a cloth that had seen the same wood a thousand times. "Both, this time of evening. Merchants who don't want to pay Slaughtered Pig prices, workers finishing a late shift. A few regulars." She tucked the cloth back over the rim of a bucket beneath the counter. "Weekends are busier. People passing through to everywhere else."

A couple of unnamed patrons occupied a far table, speaking low over their own meals. The common room held the ordinary warmth of a place where nobody was expecting trouble. Jessa's gaze drifted once to the door as it opened — a man in a work apron who raised a hand to her and settled onto a bench without ordering yet — and returned to Nicco.

"Clockmaker," she repeated, as though tasting the word. "Can't say I know one offhand in West. Doesn't mean there isn't — I just haven't had reason to notice. You might try asking down at the market stalls if anyone's seen one, or the guild hall if there is one. I've not had a guest ask for that before." She said it plainly, without apology.
